name: Guro
confidence_why: Kuznetsova 2007 and the reference description in Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017 treat Guro as a tone language without phonological word stress, the weakening of one syllable within the foot being predictable from segmental structure, whereas Vydrine 2003 read the same reduction facts as a dynamic accent beside tone while calling his observations preliminary. One further first-hand description conflicts (see the conflicting-description item); the entry follows Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017 2017.

В зависимости от структуры, в двусложной стопе может ослабляться либо первый слог (вплоть до выпадения первого гласного), либо второй (вплоть до выпадения начального согласного второго слога): tẹ́lẹ́ > tlẹ́ ‛земля’, pẹ́lẹ́pẹ́lẹ́ > plẹ́plẹ́ ‛сильный’, (в южных диалектах) lāwà > lāà ‛карман’, pálụ́ > páụ́ ‛лысина’, либо ни тот, ни другой. В синтагме ритмическая вершина (синтаксически главное слово, либо последнее слово группы) фонетически выделяется также при помощи интенсивности и длительности гласного. В Г.я. выделяется пять фонологически значимых т о н е м: три уровневые (высокая, средняя, низкая) и две контурные, или модулированные (восходящая и нисходящая). Носитель тонемы — слог.

new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Stress in the classical sense is absent in Guro; however, under the effect of reduction a metrical inequality of syllables is developing. Depending on the structure, in a disyllabic foot either the first syllable may be weakened (up to loss of the first vowel) or the second (up to loss of the initial consonant of the second syllable): tẹ́lẹ́ > tlẹ́ 'earth' ... (in southern dialects) lāwà > lāà 'pocket', pálụ́ > páụ́ 'baldness', or neither. These phenomena have no phonological significance, but in the long run the process may lead to the development of word and syntagmatic stress. Within the syntagm the rhythmic peak (the syntactic head word, or the last word of the group) is also phonetically marked by intensity and vowel duration.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Guro is a tone language (5 tonemes: H, M, L, rising, falling; TBU = syllable) with no word stress in the classical sense. Within the (maximally disyllabic) phonological foot there is structure-dependent, non-contrastive weakening of one syllable: in CVLV feet with identical vowels the first vowel reduces/deletes (CLV), in some CVV/CVLV feet with unlike vowels the second syllable weakens, and some feet show neither; the authors treat this as phonetic, predictable from segmental make-up, and not (yet) stress. Vydrine 2003 analysed the same facts as a 'dynamic accent' falling on the second syllable of CVLV feet in the great majority of cases and on the first when V1 is more open than V2, with a residual 'accentless' class; Kuznetsova 2007 and Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017 explicitly reject a phonological accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Feet meeting CVLV criteria that resist reduction (ɓēlē 'comme', túlú 'tôt'); southern dialects reduce less and show second-syllable consonant loss (lāwà > lāà); Vydrine 2003 lists 'accentless' feet with roughly equal vowels (lólú 'brouillard', lílí, kṵ̀nṵ̄) and words where intensity and length split between the two vowels.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain of the syllable-inequality is the phonological foot (pied/стопа), a unit between syllable and word; phrase level: rhythmic peak of the syntagm (head or last word) marked by intensity and duration. Description based on the Zuénoula (central) dialect zone; lexical citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: All three primary sources describe the Zuénoula (central) dialect zone of Guro (Kuznetsovas' fieldwork with Zuénoula-dialect speakers; Vydrine's informants from Gaïzra/Zuénoula, parlers mʌ and maa); the 2017 chapter notes southern dialects reduce feet less and differently. Language-level glottocode guro1248 applies; no separate dialect glottocode assigned here.

new_statements.quote: A mon avis, la notion d'accent phonologique n'est pas très fonctionnelle pour le gouro, au moins au stade actuel de son évolution. D'abord, la réduction d'une syllabe est prévisible à partir de la structure segmentale de la séquence. C'est-à-dire que des paires minimales se distinguant par l'accent ne sont pas possibles. [...] Cependant, il est important de noter qu'une inégalité hiérarchique phonologique entre les syllabes est en train de se créer en gouro dans le cadre du pied, mais aussi dans le groupe rythmique auquel le pied sert de base. Il s'agit d'un phénomène du niveau phonétique qui ressemble à l'accent lexical et syntagmatique.
new_statements.translation: In my view, the notion of phonological accent is not very functional for Guro, at least at the present stage of its evolution. First, the reduction of a syllable is predictable from the segmental structure of the sequence. That is, minimal pairs distinguished by accent are not possible. [...] However, it is important to note that a hierarchical phonological inequality between syllables is in the process of forming in Guro within the foot, and also within the rhythmic group of which the foot is the base. This is a phonetic-level phenomenon that resembles lexical and phrasal accent.
new_statements.citation: [NOT IN THE WORKS LIST; the text the conflated citation actually points at, already held by the project from the 2026-09-17 download] Kuznetsova, Natalia. 2007. Le statut fonctionnel du pied phonologique en gouro. Mandenkan 43: 13-45. Section 1 'Le système tonal du gouro' (p. 13); accent classification p. 41.

new_statements.relation_note: Same authors and same position as the existing statement from Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017 (Jazyki mira: 'Ударение в классическом смысле в Г.я. отсутствует, однако под действием редукции развивается метрическая неравноправность слогов'). Refines it by giving the argument: reduction is predictable from segmental structure, hence no minimal pairs, hence no phonological accent; and by naming the position it rejects (Vydrine 2002, 2003).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Guro is a tone language (three level tonemes in complementary distribution plus a modulated tone, sec. 1). Kuznetsova rejects a phonological word accent: syllable reduction inside the disyllabic foot is predictable from the segmental make-up of the sequence, so accent can never distinguish words; outside prototypical feet the reduction is weak and unstable (p. 41). What exists is an emerging, phonetic-level inequality of syllables within the foot and the rhythmic group, which only resembles lexical/phrasal accent. She explicitly answers Vydrine 2002/2003, who had posited a dynamic accent (p. 41: 'Les modèles différents de la réduction ont amené Vydrine à supposer l'existence de l'accent en gouro'). Data: young speakers of the Zuénoula dialect (fn. 3, p. 13).
new_statements.exceptions: none stated; reduction is described as weak and unstable outside prototypical feet (p. 41)
new_statements.identity_note: Kuznetsova 2007 describes the speech of young speakers of the Zuénoula dialect (fn. 3, p. 13). Vydrine 2003 works with informant Doubi Benjamin (p. 112) and compares Le Saout's and Benoist's recordings; he mentions possible dialectal variants for some tonal realisations but does not tie the accent observations to a named dialect. The listed work (Mandenkan 43: 47-59) is about Mwan (mwan1250), a different South Mande language.

new_statements.quote: 3. L'autre divergence concerne l'existence en gouro d'un accent dynamique, ignorée dans la description de Le Saout [...]. Dans les « pieds » dissyllabiques à voyelles identiques (type CVLV), c'est la deuxième syllabe qui porte l'accent dans la grande majorité des cas (d'où la réduction de la première voyelle, parfois jusqu'à son élimination compete). Dans les « pieds » à voyelles différentes, l'emplacement de l'accent varie d'un mot à l'autre, et la voyelle non accentuée est le plus souvent réduite. Il semble que la première voyelle tend à être accentuée quand elle est plus ouverte que la deuxième, la deuxième voyelle étant accentuée dans tous les autres cas.
new_statements.translation: 3. The other divergence concerns the existence in Guro of a dynamic accent, ignored in Le Saout's description [...]. In disyllabic 'feet' with identical vowels (type CVLV), it is the second syllable that carries the accent in the great majority of cases (hence the reduction of the first vowel, sometimes to its complete elimination). In 'feet' with different vowels, the position of the accent varies from word to word, and the unaccented vowel is most often reduced. It seems that the first vowel tends to be accented when it is more open than the second, the second vowel being accented in all other cases.

new_statements.relation_note: Vydrine posits a word-level dynamic accent with partly predictable placement, whereas the catalog's existing statement (Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017) and Kuznetsova 2007 say stress in the classical sense is absent and the syllable inequality is a phonetic effect of reduction. The disagreement is largely one of status (phonological accent vs. predictable phonetic prominence): both describe the same second-syllable prominence in CVLV feet and the same vowel-openness effect. Vydrine himself labels his account preliminary, and Kuznetsova 2007 p. 41 rebuts it explicitly.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Guro has tone (three level tonemes, p. 112) and, according to Vydrine, additionally a dynamic accent (intensity plus vowel length) within the disyllabic foot, offered as 'observations préliminaires' (p. 91). Placement: in CVLV feet with identical vowels the second syllable is accented and the first vowel reduces; in feet with different vowels the first vowel is accented when it is more open than the second, otherwise the second. Conclusions p. 112: 'le gouro a, à côté du ton, un accent dynamique dont l'emplacement est partiellement déterminé par les types des combinaisons vocaliques à l'intérieur du « pied ». Un « pied » dissyllabique peut porter l'accent sur la première syllabe, sur la deuxième syllabe, ou ne pas avoir d'accent'. The accented syllable also carries the main part of the tonal contour (p. 91).
new_statements.secondary_stress: none stated; phrase-level accent noted: in e miania 'il dépasse' the dynamic accent falls on the pronoun without reducing the verb's vowels; relation between phrase and word accent left for future study (p. 92)
new_statements.exceptions: a third class of feet where the first vowel is louder but the second is not reduced (lolu 'brouillard', lili, kunu, mwene) and words where force and length split between the two vowels; provisionally treated as 'mots sans accent' (p. 92)

The listed work (Mandenkan 43: 47-59) is about Mwan (mwan1250), a different South Mande language.

tone_statements.quote: Guro has a system of five tones (H – high, M – mid, L – low, F – falling, R – rising) which mark every syllable and fulfill numerous lexical and grammatical functions.
tone_statements.locator: p. 44, sec. 2.1 'Structure of a featural foot'
tone_statements.summary: 5 tones H M L F R, syllable TBU; onset-conditioned tone distribution (raising vs depressor consonants); contours mainly on monosyllabic feet; 4 tonal classes of nouns with mobile/assimilating initial tones.

Rossijskaja lingvističeskaja èkspedicija v Kot-d'Ivuar i orfografičeskie reformy v južnyx jazykax mande [Russian linguistic field trips to Côte d'Ivoire and orthography reforms in the South Mande languages]. Kunstkamera 2019, no. 4(6): 107-121. doi:10.31250/2618-8619-2019-4(6)-107-121
tone_statements.quote: ... в синхронии следует констатировать завершившееся расщепление тонов, так что тональная система оказывается трехуровневой (Выдрин 2002), выделяются также два модулированных тона — восходящий и нисходящий (Кузнецова, Кузнецова 2017: 770). ... Тоны обозначаются при помощи диакритических знаков: акута (высокий тон), грависа (низкий тон), средний тон выражается отсутствием диакритики. Для обозначения модулированных тонов используется циркумфлекс (падающий тон) и умлаут (восходящий тон).
tone_statements.translation: ... synchronically one must recognise a completed tone split, so that the tonal system turns out to be three-level (Vydrin 2002); two modulated tones are also distinguished, rising and falling (Kuznetsova, Kuznetsova 2017: 770). ... Tones are marked with diacritics: acute (high tone), grave (low tone); mid tone is expressed by absence of a diacritic. For the modulated tones the circumflex (falling tone) and umlaut (rising tone) are used.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 109-110, section 'ГУРО', paragraphs 'Новая орфография гуро' and the tone-marking paragraph after Table 1
tone_statements.summary: Guro has three level tones (high, mid, low) after a completed tone split, plus two modulated tones (rising, falling), per Vydrin 2002 and Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017; Le Saout's older two-tone analysis with depressor consonants is historical. Nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: Kuznetsova, Olga V. [Кузнецова, Ольга Васильевна]. 2013. Glagol v jazyke guro [Глагол в языке гуро / The verb in the Guro language]. Dissertation for the degree of kandidat filologičeskix nauk (speciality 10.02.20), St. Petersburg (Glottolog: Saint Petersburg State University). 210 pp.
tone_statements.quote: В глагольной морфологии языка гуро важную роль играют тональные изменения. Эту черту гуро разделяет с другими южными манде, однако количество глагольных форм, образование которых сопровождается изменением тона, больше, а сложность правил реализации тональных морфем в гуро несколько выше, чем в других языках группы.
tone_statements.translation: Tonal changes play an important role in the verbal morphology of Guro. Guro shares this feature with the other South Mande languages, but the number of verb forms whose formation is accompanied by a change of tone is larger, and the rules realising the tonal morphemes are somewhat more complex in Guro than in the other languages of the group.
tone_statements.locator: Introduction, 'Положения, выносимые на защиту', no. 1 (dissercat record page)
tone_statements.summary: Verbal grammatical tone: lexical verb tones, mobile tone model, tonal verb classes, 3SG.NSBJ pronoun fused as tone.

tone_statements.citation: Kuznetsova, Olga V. [Кузнецова О. В.]. 2010. Perexod postglagol'nogo mestoimenija v jazyke guro v tonal'nuju morfemu [Переход постглагольного местоимения в языке гуро в тональную морфему / The change of a postverbal pronoun into a tonal morpheme in Guro]. In: Materialy Sed'moj Konferencii po tipologii i grammatike dlja molodyx issledovatelej (Acta Linguistica Petropolitana. Trudy ILI RAN, vol. 6, part 3), 85-89. St. Petersburg: Nauka.
tone_statements.quote: В языке гуро тоны глагольной основы участвуют в выражении TAM-категорий и полярности наряду с местоимениями и показателями конструкций. Глаголы делятся на 11 групп (тональных классов), в зависимости от того, каким образом они изменяют тоны глагольной основы в различных грамматических контекстах. ... H — высокий тон, M — средний тон, L — низкий тон, R — восходящий тон, F — падающий тон.
tone_statements.translation: In Guro the tones of the verb stem take part in expressing TAM categories and polarity, along with pronouns and construction markers. Verbs divide into 11 groups (tonal classes) according to how they change the tones of the verb stem in different grammatical contexts. ... H = high tone, M = mid tone, L = low tone, R = rising tone, F = falling tone.
tone_statements.locator: p. 85, opening paragraph; and p. 89, key to Table 1 'Тональная морфология глаголов'
tone_statements.summary: Verbal tonal morphology paper: five tone labels (high, mid, low, rising, falling) given as the key to a table of 11 verb tone classes; verb tones may copy the preceding word's final tone; the postverbal 3SG pronoun can surface as a bare tone change on the verb (a tonal morpheme). Nothing on stress.

tone_statements.quote: it proves that the system of modern Guro contains three phonological level tones rather than two. ... Our own research shows that there are two additional phonological contour tones, rising and falling, that cannot be reduced to a combination of level tones. ... we propose to mark tones with accents over the vowels according to the current IPA practice: acute accent for the high tone, grave accent for the low tone, absence of any mark for the middle tone. For the rising tone, a haček could be used (séě ‘shrimp’) ... For the falling tone, we propose the use of a circumflex
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (H, M, L; after Vydrine 2003) plus rising and falling unit tonemes, argued from loanwords, CVV feet and FF sequences; 16 patterns on disyllabic feet (p. 196); lower register after voiced obstruents; tonal morphology on genitive heads (p. 199). 100+ tone-marked forms. No stress.

tone_statements.citation: Konoshenko, Maria. 2022. Tones and paradigms: a study of grammatical tones in Mande verbal inflection. Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 43(2): 165-197. doi:10.1515/jall-2022-8900
tone_statements.quote: Another Southern Mande language, Guro, presents a highly complex case with ITCs based on the lexical tone of the verb and the initial consonant type (Kuznetsova and Kuznetsova 2017: 834).
tone_statements.check: quotation from a journal article located by the 2026-09-24 journal search, not yet verified by a second reading
tone_statements.summary: Guro has replacive grammatical tones forming inflectional tonal classes: raising in the Perfective, lowering in the Imperfective and Negative Imperfective (both with suffixes), the class depending on lexical tone and initial consonant type. Adds to the catalog's entry of five tonemes with lexical and grammatical functions; nothing on stress.

readall_conflicts: Vydrine 2003 (Mandenkan 38: 91-92, 112) posits a dynamic accent alongside tone, second-syllable in CVLV feet and openness-driven elsewhere, with a class of accentless words; Kuznetsova 2007 (Mandenkan 43: 41) answers him directly: reduction is predictable from segmental structure, no minimal pairs by accent, so 'la notion d'accent phonologique n'est pas très fonctionnelle pour le gouro', only a phonetic-level inequality of syllables that resembles accent. Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017 (the catalog's existing statement) restate the 2007 position. The listed Perekhvalskaya item is not a third voice: it is a mis-citation and is about Mwan. The disagreement is about phonological status, not about which syllable is prominent.

В зависимости от структуры, в двусложной стопе может ослабляться либо первый слог (вплоть до выпадения первого гласного), либо второй (вплоть до выпадения начального согласного второго слога): tẹ́lẹ́ > tlẹ́ ‛земля’ ... (в южных диалектах) lāwà > lāà ‛карман’, pálụ́ > páụ́ ‛лысина’, либо ни тот, ни другой. Фонологической значимости эти явления не имеют, но в перспективе процесс может привести к развитию словесного и синтагматического ударения. В синтагме ритмическая вершина (синтаксически главное слово, либо последнее слово группы) фонетически выделяется также при помощи интенсивности и длительности гласного.

sources.citation: [NOT IN THE WORKS LIST; already held by the project from the 2026-09-17 download, read because Kuznetsova 2007 argues against it] Vydrine, Valentin. 2003. La phonologie gouro : deux décennies après Le Saout. Mandenkan 38: 89-113. Sec. 3 (pp. 91-92) and sec. 9 Conclusions (p. 112).
sources.quote: 3. L'autre divergence concerne l'existence en gouro d'un accent dynamique, ignorée dans la description de Le Saout [...]. Dans les « pieds » dissyllabiques à voyelles identiques (type CVLV), c'est la deuxième syllabe qui porte l'accent dans la grande majorité des cas (d'où la réduction de la première voyelle, parfois jusqu'à son élimination compete). Dans les « pieds » à voyelles différentes, l'emplacement de l'accent varie d'un mot à l'autre, et la voyelle non accentuée est le plus souvent réduite. Il semble que la première voyelle tend à être accentuée quand elle est plus ouverte que la deuxième, la deuxième voyelle étant accentuée dans tous les autres cas.
sources.locator: sec. 3, p. 91 (p. 3 of 25); classes and phrase accent p. 92 (p. 4); Conclusions p. 112 (p. 24)
sources.note: Vydrine posits a word-level dynamic accent with partly predictable placement, whereas the catalog's existing statement (Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017) and Kuznetsova 2007 say stress in the classical sense is absent and the syllable inequality is a phonetic effect of reduction. The disagreement is largely one of status (phonological accent vs. predictable phonetic prominence): both describe the same second-syllable prominence in CVLV feet and the same vowel-openness effect. Vydrine himself labels his account preliminary, and Kuznetsova 2007 p. 41 rebuts it explicitly.

sources.citation: [NOT IN THE WORKS LIST; the text the conflated citation actually points at, already held by the project from the 2026-09-17 download] Kuznetsova, Natalia. 2007. Le statut fonctionnel du pied phonologique en gouro. Mandenkan 43: 13-45. Section 1 'Le système tonal du gouro' (p. 13); accent classification p. 41.
sources.quote: A mon avis, la notion d'accent phonologique n'est pas très fonctionnelle pour le gouro, au moins au stade actuel de son évolution. D'abord, la réduction d'une syllabe est prévisible à partir de la structure segmentale de la séquence. C'est-à-dire que des paires minimales se distinguant par l'accent ne sont pas possibles. [...] Cependant, il est important de noter qu'une inégalité hiérarchique phonologique entre les syllabes est en train de se créer en gouro dans le cadre du pied, mais aussi dans le groupe rythmique auquel le pied sert de base. Il s'agit d'un phénomène du niveau phonétique qui ressemble à l'accent lexical et syntagmatique.
sources.note: Same authors and same position as the existing statement from Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova 2017 (Jazyki mira: 'Ударение в классическом смысле в Г.я. отсутствует, однако под действием редукции развивается метрическая неравноправность слогов'). Refines it by giving the argument: reduction is predictable from segmental structure, hence no minimal pairs, hence no phonological accent; and by naming the position it rejects (Vydrine 2002, 2003).

sources.citation: Vydrine, Valentin. 2003. La phonologie gouro : deux décennies après Le Saout. Mandenkan 38: 89-113.
sources.note: Sec. 3 and Conclusions: argues Guro has, besides tone, a dynamic accent (intensity + vowel length) ignored by Le Saout and all earlier descriptions; in CVLV feet with identical vowels the second syllable carries the accent in the great majority of cases (first vowel reduced, sometimes deleted); with different vowels placement varies word to word, first vowel tending to be accented when more open than the second, otherwise the second; a third group of 'accentless' feet; placement 'partiellement déterminé' by vowel combinations; phrase accent unstudied. Explicitly preliminary.

sources.citation: Kuznetsova, Natalia. 2007. Le statut fonctionnel du pied phonologique en gouro. Mandenkan 43: 13-45.
sources.note: pp. 41-42: rejects Vydrine's phonological accent: 'la notion d'accent phonologique n'est pas très fonctionnelle pour le gouro'; syllable reduction is predictable from segmental structure, no minimal pairs by accent are possible, reduction outside prototypical feet is weak and unstable; a phonetic-level syllable inequality resembling lexical and syntagmatic accent is emerging within the foot and rhythmic group. Data: Zuénoula dialect.
sources.venue: Mandenkan: bull. semestriel d'études linguistiques mandé 43

sources.citation: Kuznetsova, Natalia V. & Kuznetsova, Olga V. 2017. Guro jazyk [Guro]. In: Vydrin V., Mazurova Yu., Kibrik A., Markus E. (eds.), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, 765-877. St. Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija.
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2 (pp. 769-770): stress in the classical sense is absent in Guro; under foot reduction a metrical inequality of syllables is developing (either first or second syllable of a disyllabic foot may weaken, depending on structure, or neither); these phenomena have no phonological significance but may lead in future to word and syntagmatic stress; in the syntagm the rhythmic peak (head word or last word) is marked by intensity and vowel duration. Five tonemes (H, M, L, rising, falling), tone-bearing unit = syllable.

sources.quote: В языке гуро тоны глагольной основы участвуют в выражении TAM-категорий и полярности наряду с местоимениями и показателями конструкций. Глаголы делятся на 11 групп (тональных классов), в зависимости от того, каким образом они изменяют тоны глагольной основы в различных грамматических контекстах. ... Nothing on stress.

tone.translation: In Guro the tones of the verb stem take part in expressing TAM categories and polarity, along with pronouns and construction markers. Verbs divide into 11 groups (tonal classes) according to how they change the tones of the verb stem in different grammatical contexts. ... H = high tone, M = mid tone, L = low tone, R = rising tone, F = falling tone.

tone.quote: Among Southern Mande languages, Guro [iso:goa] presents the most complex tonal behavior that we have encountered. As described in Kuznetsova & Kuznetsova (2017: 784), THM is present, but patterns differ between multiple nominal lexical tonal classes. Crucially, however, THM usually involves tone lowering on W2. For example: /zã̀/ ‘host’ + /lị̄/ ‘woman’ → [zã̀#lị̀] ‘female host.’
